text: #OTD 30 years ago, Astronomy Picture of the Day made its first post. Each day it provides a new image for a bit of inspiration. So, if you need more than a #MondayMotivation, you can check them out any day of the week. https://t.co/FDhYwbOgCE https://t.co/yxybMZQeJe

mediaDetails.ext_alt_text: This composite image shows an open star cluster called the Coronet Cluster in X-rays from our Chandra telescope (purple) and infrared emission from Spitzer (orange, green, and cyan). The image is dominated by a glowing circle with wispy clouds in hues of pink, purple, and blue. Slightly off-center is a bright group of white stars, surrounded by a small irregular halo of greenish-blue material. Other stars, large and small, dot the image from edge to edge. The image is watermarked with the words “Credit: NASA/CXC/JPL-Caltech/CfA.”
